title: 中国菜的绝活③北京烤鸭·先给鸭子吹口气 | Signature Skill P3 · Air-Blown for Crispy Skin 🦆
description:
吃烤鸭，你蘸甜面酱，还是蘸白糖？ / Peking duck: sweet bean sauce, or sugar?

第③集·吹与片 —— 「中国菜的绝活」系列。烤之前，师傅先给鸭子吹一口气。
P3 · Blow & Carve — from the series The Signature Skill. Before roasting, the cook blows air into the duck.

为什么吹气？空气被压进鸭皮和鸭肉之间，让皮肉分离——只有分离了，皮才能烤得又薄又脆。北京烤鸭分两大流派：挂炉派用枣木等果木明火烤（全聚德，1864年创号），焖炉派不见明火、全靠炉壁热力（便宜坊，可上溯明永乐1416年，早四百多年）。皮要烤成枣红透亮才算成。上桌前片鸭：讲究的一只片成108片（数字借梁山一百单八将），常见72到108片，片片带皮带肉。两派技艺均为国家级非物质文化遗产。
Why blow? Air is forced between the skin and the meat so they separate — only then can the skin roast thin and crisp. Peking duck has two schools: the hung-oven style roasts over an open fruitwood fire (Quanjude, founded 1864), while the closed-oven style uses no open flame, only heat from the oven walls (Bianyifang, traceable to 1416 — 400+ years older). The skin must roast to a glossy jujube-red. Then it's carved: a proper duck yields 108 slices (a number borrowed from the 108 heroes of Liangshan), commonly 72–108, each with both skin and meat. Both techniques are national intangible cultural heritage.
